files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Owner: N. Vartanian. Complete in sequence; no skipping ahead.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; some months all payroll runs pay in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to prevent duplication. If the amortization is missing, book June as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying the GL to ensure it has not already been recorded.
5. Verify the expense coding on all June vendor bills by comparing the bill documents with the GL. Reclass anything miscoded to the correct expense account.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Vantage Loop Inc. began in 2019 after two operations-minded software colleagues grew tired of watching customer teams manage recurring work through scattered spreadsheets, inbox threads, and improvised checklists. They built a lightweight prototype that made handoffs visible without forcing users into a heavyweight project-management system. Early customers helped shape the product into a practical SaaS platform for coordinating repeatable workflows, approvals, reminders, and status reporting.

The company now sells hosted workflow software to small and midsize organizations with operationally complex teams. Customers use it for onboarding, compliance routines, service delivery, campaign coordination, and other processes where ownership and timing matter. The product is deliberately straightforward: configurable enough for administrators, but familiar enough that occasional users can participate with little training.

The team has a distinctly hands-on flavor. Engineers join customer calls, support staff maintain unusually detailed implementation notes, and the commercial group prefers useful demonstrations over polished jargon. Finance and administration remain lean, so month-end work is structured around clear schedules, source documents, and repeatable review steps.

Vantage Loop Inc. is an ordinary going concern focused on steady product improvement, dependable service, and disciplined growth. Current priorities include sharpening its market position, improving customer education, strengthening partner channels, and making internal reporting more consistent as the business matures.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction
Position Vantage Loop Inc. as the practical workflow layer for teams that have outgrown shared spreadsheets but do not want a complicated enterprise rollout. Keep the message concrete: clearer ownership, fewer missed handoffs, and faster adoption.

## Priorities
- Refresh the core brand language and visual system without changing the company’s approachable tone.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, built around real operating problems rather than broad product tours.
- Pilot a co-marketing program with selected implementation and advisory partners.
- Publish short customer stories that show how repeatable workflows improve day-to-day coordination.
- Tighten the path from campaign response to product demonstration and follow-up.

## Quarterly sequence
### Q3
Complete messaging work, update high-traffic web pages, prepare the webinar format, and recruit partners for the pilot. Build a reusable campaign kit for sales and customer success.

### Q4
Expand the strongest webinar topics, launch partner-led content, and test industry-specific landing pages. Use customer questions to shape practical guides and demonstration scripts.

## Measurement
Track qualified engagement, webinar attendance and follow-through, partner-sourced conversations, content-assisted demonstrations, and movement through the evaluation process. Review results jointly with sales and customer success.

## Open items
Confirm campaign ownership, creative capacity, partner participation, and final resourcing after the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from your predecessor

N. Vartanian — a few things that will save you some hunting:

- The bank tends to post its own fees and service charges near the end of the statement. We have historically booked those during close rather than during the month, so do not assume they are already in the ledger.
- June moved quickly, and the expense coding on vendor bills may be off. Compare the entries to the source documents and treat the files in bills/ as authoritative.
- The budget was fixed early, at the start of Q2. The one-off June items were never included, and they should explain most of the larger budget-to-actual variances.
- Payroll timing matters this month: the back half of June pays in early July. The payroll register contains the applicable dates.
